images.filename: First airplane takeoff from a warship.jpg
images.caption:
First airplane takeoff from a warship
Eugene Burton Ely flies his Curtiss pusher biplane from USS Birmingham (Scout Cruiser No. 2), in Hampton Roads, Virginia, during the afternoon of 14 November 1910.

USS Roe (Destroyer No. 24), serving as plane guard, is visible in the background.
images.alt:

images.filename: Bridge of a drift collection vessel on the Elizabeth River.jpg
images.caption: Art Kohn, from WAVY-TV 10, interviews Jeff Gibbs, a Norfolk District boat captain, while he patrols the Elizabeth River looking for debris in the water after Hurricane Irene hit the area.  The Hampton Roads Drift Removal Program, which takes place all year long, ensures the federal navigation channel is safe for commercial shipping and boaters.  (U.S. Army Photo/Patrick Bloodgood)
